placeholder.title: Coming soon
placeholder.description: This section is part of a later milestone. The app shell is ready; the data will appear here once the agent is connected.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Changes apply immediately and are saved for your Windows user.
appearance.reduceMotionHint: Turns off transitions, counting numbers and pulses. Off by default and independent of Windows: Windows Server ships with visual effects off, and PacketWard ignores that.

startup.title: Startup
startup.description: Choose whether PacketWard opens by itself.
startup.autostartHint: Opens minimized to the system tray when you sign in. The agent runs regardless.

language.title: Language
language.description: Automatic follows the Windows display language.
language.label: Interface language

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Which alerts pop up a Windows notification. Every alert always appears in the Alerts inbox.
notifications.hint: Notifications are shown by this app, so they appear while it is running (minimized to the tray counts). The agent keeps protecting the server either way.

network.title: Network
network.description: How PacketWard reaches the internet for update checks, speed tests, GeoIP and blocklist downloads, and AbuseIPDB.
network.hint: http://, https:// or socks5:// with a host and port. Never put the user name or password in the address: use the fields below.
network.restart: The change applies when the PacketWard service restarts (Services → PacketWard → Restart).
network.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved password
network.credentialsSaved: Credentials saved for {user}. They live in the Windows Credential Manager, not in any file.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: PacketWard never installs an update without your confirmation. It looks for new versions when it starts and every 24 hours; you can turn that off.
updates.betaHint: Pre-releases for testing; you also receive stable releases that supersede them.
updates.checkOnStartHint: On by default. One small request to GitHub a few seconds after the app opens and then every 24 hours. It only looks: nothing is downloaded or installed until you press the button.
updates.upToDate: You are running the latest version of this channel.
updates.notConfigured: Updates are not configured in this build: it has no update signing key, so it cannot verify or install updates. Download new versions from the PacketWard releases page instead.
updates.privacy: A check only downloads a small version file from GitHub. Installers are verified against the signing key built into this app before they run. The installer stops the PacketWard service, replaces the files and starts it again; your settings and rules are kept.

about.title: About PacketWard
about.tagline: Network defense and diagnostics for Windows Server VPS and RDP machines.
about.madeBy: Built by XeroHost and released as open source.

credits.title: Credits and licenses
credits.geoip: GeoIP data: DB-IP Lite, CC BY 4.0 (db-ip.com).
credits.icons: Icons: the free Hugeicons set, MIT.
credits.fonts: Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque, Geist and JetBrains Mono, SIL OFL 1.1.
credits.ui: Components: Reka UI and shadcn-vue, MIT. Charts: Apache ECharts, Apache-2.0.
credits.note: Every dependency is checked for compatibility with the GPL-3.0 license of PacketWard. Animate UI was not used: its Commons Clause license is not compatible.
credits.maps: Flags: country-flag-icons, MIT. World map: Natural Earth (public domain) via world-atlas and topojson-client, ISC; country codes: i18n-iso-countries, MIT.

notInstalled.title: The PacketWard agent is not installed
notInstalled.body: PacketWard needs its background service to watch your network, even while you are disconnected. Install it to continue.

stopped.title: The PacketWard agent is not running
stopped.body: The background service is installed but stopped, so nothing is being monitored. Start it to continue.

starting.title: Starting the PacketWard agent…
starting.body: This usually takes a few seconds.

groupMissing.title: Your account cannot reach the agent yet
groupMissing.body: The “PacketWard Operators” group does not exist. Repair the installation to create it and add your account.

notMember.title: Your account is not allowed to use the agent
notMember.body: Only administrators and members of the “PacketWard Operators” group can connect. Repair the installation to add your account.

signOutRequired.title: Sign out of Windows and sign back in
signOutRequired.body: Your account is in the “PacketWard Operators” group, but Windows only applies this when you sign in. Disconnecting and reconnecting Remote Desktop is not enough: sign out completely, then open PacketWard again.

unexplained.title: The agent refused the connection
unexplained.body: Your account looks allowed, yet access was denied. Try Repair; if it keeps happening, check the agent log in C:\ProgramData\PacketWard\logs.

agentOutdated.title: The agent is out of date
agentOutdated.body: The installed agent is older than this app and cannot communicate with it. Update PacketWard.

uiOutdated.title: This app is out of date
uiOutdated.body: The agent is newer than this app and cannot communicate with it. Update PacketWard.

error.title: Could not connect to the agent
error.body: Something unexpected stopped the connection. Repair can fix most cases.

unavailable.uacHint: Windows will ask for administrator permission.
unavailable.cancelled: The Windows permission prompt was declined, so nothing changed.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Live connection to the PacketWard agent service.

dashboard.oldAgent: The installed agent is older than this app and does not report traffic or connections. Update PacketWard.

tiles.connectionsHint: {total} in total · {waiting} waiting to close · {half} half-open

chart.title: Traffic, last 5 minutes
chart.empty: Waiting for data from the agent…

topRemote.title: Top remote addresses
topRemote.description: Who holds the most connections to this machine right now.

adapters.title: Network adapters
adapters.description: Only real adapters are added to the totals; tunnels and VPNs are shown apart.

rdp.title: Remote Desktop
rdp.description: Sessions on this machine and the addresses they connect from.
rdp.none: Nobody is connected through Remote Desktop.
rdp.peers: Connected to the RDP port from
rdp.note: These are addresses with an open connection to the RDP port. That includes anyone who has not signed in yet, so it is not proof of a legitimate session. The address a client reports for itself can differ (NAT, VPN).
rdp.trustedTitle: Addresses with a successful RDP logon (last {days} days)
rdp.trustedDescription: These are the addresses the Guardian will never block. A bot that only connects or fails to sign in never appears here.
rdp.trustedLoading: Reading recent logons from the event log…
rdp.trustedUnavailable: Cannot read the Security event log: no address can be learned.
rdp.trustedEmpty: No successful RDP logon found in the event log for this period.

protection.title: Protection
protection.off: The Guardian is off. PacketWard watches but never blocks.
protection.monitor: Monitoring: it reports what it would block and blocks nothing.
protection.active: Active: attackers are blocked automatically, for a limited time.

connections.rdpBadgeTip: Has an open connection to the Remote Desktop port
connections.truncated: The agent sent only the first {n} rows to stay within its size limit.
connections.unsupported: The installed agent is older than this app and cannot provide the connection list. Update PacketWard.
connections.failed: Could not read the connection list from the agent. It will try again.
connections.rdpTrustedBadgeTip: Connected to the RDP port and has a successful RDP logon

audit.successOff: Windows is not auditing successful logons: PacketWard cannot learn which RDP clients are legitimate, so the Guardian could not protect them.
audit.successUnknown: The audit policy for successful logons could not be read: PacketWard cannot tell whether RDP logons are recorded.
audit.failureOff: Windows is not auditing failed logons: RDP brute-force attacks cannot be detected.
audit.failureUnknown: The audit policy for failed logons could not be read: RDP brute-force detection may not work.
audit.feedUnavailable: The Security event log cannot be read, so successful RDP logons are not being learned.
audit.howToFix: Turn both on from an administrator shell:

errors.notConnected: The agent is not connected. Start it and try again.
errors.unsupported: The installed agent is older than this app and does not provide diagnostics. Update the agent.
errors.busy: Too many diagnostics are running at once. Stop one and try again.
errors.modeUnavailableHint: UDP and TCP traces read the replies through a packet capture. The built-in capture works when the agent runs as administrator, and installing Npcap (npcap.com) improves it. PacketWard does not include Npcap. ICMP traces always work.

ping.hint: Sends ICMP echo requests to measure reachability, latency and jitter.

mtr.hint: Traces the route to a host and measures loss and latency at every router, like MTR. Use Copy report to send the result to support.
mtr.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
mtr.rateLimitedTip: Later hops are clean: this router probably only limits its ICMP replies.
mtr.rateLimitedNote: Loss here is not carried to the next hops, so this router is probably just rate-limiting its replies, not dropping traffic.
mtr.packetSizeTcp: A TCP SYN carries no data, so the size does not apply.
mtr.agentTooOld: The installed agent is older than this app: UDP and TCP traces, the interval, IPv6 and export need an agent update.

export.failed: The export could not be saved or copied.

dns.hint: Looks up DNS records with the system resolver or a public one, to tell a DNS problem from a network problem.
dns.name: Name

port.hint: Tries to connect from this machine to a host and port. To test whether this server is reachable from outside, run the check from another machine.

explain.closed: The host answered and refused the connection: nothing is listening there.
explain.filtered: No answer at all. A firewall is probably dropping the traffic, or the host is down.
explain.inconclusive: UDP has no handshake: no reply does not prove the port is closed, nor open.

local.hint: What this machine is listening on. A port reachable from all interfaces is exposed to the network unless a firewall blocks it.

traffic.blind: The capture sees what this server sends but nothing it receives, so flood detection from capture is unreliable here. Connection, bandwidth and RDP-logon detection are not affected. On Windows the firewall can hide inbound packets from a raw-socket capture; installing Npcap avoids this.
traffic.notRunning: Packet capture is not running, so there are no per-packet statistics.
traffic.droppedHint: Counted, never hidden: lost to a full queue or by the driver
traffic.untrackedHint: Packets from sources the table had no room for (still in the rates)
traffic.chartTitle: Traffic seen by the capture (last 2 minutes)
traffic.talkersHint: Who sent the most packets to this server in the last second.

backend.title: Capture backend
backend.licenseNote: PacketWard does not include Npcap (its license does not allow redistribution). If you install it yourself from npcap.com, PacketWard uses it automatically.

record.title: Record to a file
record.hint: Saves packets to a .pcapng file you can open in Wireshark. By default only the first 128 bytes of each packet are kept (headers, not content).
record.name: File name
record.fullWarning: Full packets include the content of the traffic (for example unencrypted passwords or messages). Tick this only if you need it and will keep the file private.
record.ringNote: Keeps recording until you stop it, deleting the oldest part so the files never exceed 200 MB.

files.title: Recorded files
files.retention: readable by administrators only; files older than 7 days are deleted automatically.

bundle.title: Support bundle
bundle.hint: A zip for XeroHost support: versions, traffic summary, adapters, recent logs and an optional short traffic sample. Look at exactly what it contains before saving. It is saved on this computer only and never uploaded.
bundle.anonymizeNote: Addresses of this server and its name are replaced by placeholders in the text files. The traffic sample cannot be anonymized, so it is left out.
bundle.hidden: {count} local addresses will be replaced with placeholders.
bundle.binary: Binary file: it is recorded when you save.
bundle.attach: Attach this file to your support ticket.

alerts.failed: The alert list could not be read from the agent.
alerts.none: No alerts. When PacketWard sees a flood, a scan or a brute-force attempt it will show up here.

summary.rdp_new_logon: Successful Remote Desktop logon from a new address

explain.syn_flood: One address is opening a huge number of connections it never completes, to exhaust the server.
explain.syn_flood_distributed: Many addresses are opening connections they never complete.
explain.udp_flood: One address is sending a very high volume of UDP packets.
explain.udp_flood_distributed: A very high volume of UDP packets is arriving from many addresses.
explain.icmp_flood: One address is sending a very high volume of ping packets.
explain.icmp_flood_distributed: A very high volume of ping packets is arriving from many addresses.
explain.port_scan_vertical: One address is probing many ports of this server, looking for something to attack.
explain.port_scan_horizontal: One address is probing the same port on many hosts.
explain.conn_flood: One address holds or opens an unusual number of connections.
explain.rdp_brute_force: One address keeps failing to log in over Remote Desktop: someone is guessing passwords.
explain.volumetric_attack: Incoming traffic is using almost all of the network link.
explain.rdp_new_logon: Someone logged in over Remote Desktop from an address that had never logged in before. If it was you on a new connection, ignore this; if not, change the password and review the sessions.

blocks.hint: Addresses blocked through Windows Firewall, by you or by the Guardian. Many addresses share a few rules.
blocks.refusedBroad: not blocked: the range is too wide (wider than /8 for IPv4).

purge.title: Remove all PacketWard rules
purge.hint: Deletes every firewall rule PacketWard created (blocks, allow rules, RDP rules) and nothing else. Use it to get back to a clean state.
purge.phrase: If PacketWard restricts Remote Desktop, type: {phrase}

rules.foreignNote: Rules that PacketWard did not create are shown for reference. Changing one asks for confirmation first.
rules.name: Name

confirm.delete: Delete the rule “{name}”? This cannot be undone.

rules.foreignWarning: This rule was not created by PacketWard. You are changing a rule of Windows or another program.
rules.lockoutPhrase: This can cut you off from Remote Desktop. Type: {phrase}
rules.truncated: Only the first rules are shown; narrow the search.

protected.hint: These addresses are never blocked, by you or by the Guardian: this machine, its gateway and DNS servers, every address with a successful Remote Desktop logon, and the lists below.
protected.allowlistHint: Your own addresses or ranges (one per line).
protected.managementHint: Ranges XeroHost uses to manage the server (one per line).

protectedReasons.rdp_client: Remote Desktop client with a successful logon

dialog.title: Block this address?
dialog.consequence: Windows Firewall will drop all traffic from it. Addresses you rely on (gateway, DNS, trusted Remote Desktop clients, allowlist) are refused.

explain.off: The Guardian does nothing. Alerts still appear; nothing is blocked automatically.
explain.monitor: The Guardian watches and records what it would block, without blocking anything. Review the report below, then switch to Active.
explain.active: The Guardian blocks attackers automatically for a limited time, with a limit per hour. Blocks expire by themselves and can be removed any time.

active.warning: Automatic blocking can block a legitimate address by mistake. Your Remote Desktop clients, gateway and DNS are protected, and every block expires.
active.report: In the last 24 hours the Guardian would have blocked {count} address(es).
active.reviewed: I reviewed the Monitor report and want automatic blocking.

status.circuitNote: The hourly limit of automatic blocks was reached, so the Guardian stopped blocking. It resumes when the hour has passed. If this looks like a big attack, review the alerts.

policy.title: Policy
policy.ladder: Block durations in minutes (first offence, then repeats)
policy.hint: Password guessing against Remote Desktop is blocked from Medium severity; everything else from the severity chosen here.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.hint: Why each address was (or would have been) blocked or left alone.

pending.explain: Confirm it from a new connection within {seconds} s or it will be reverted automatically.

open_to_any.title: Remote Desktop is reachable from any address
open_to_any.fix: Restrict it to the addresses you use (below). Until then every bot on the Internet can try your passwords.

nla_off.title: Network Level Authentication is not required
nla_off.fix: Require it: attackers must authenticate before a session is even created. Turn it on below.

weak_security_layer.title: The RDP security layer is the old one
weak_security_layer.fix: Set the security layer to Negotiate or TLS in Group Policy (Remote Desktop Session Host → Security).

default_port.title: Remote Desktop uses the default port 3389
default_port.fix: A different port avoids most automatic scans (it is not a defense by itself). Change it below, and connect to the new port afterwards.

no_lockout.title: No account lockout
no_lockout.fix: Optional. Blocking the attacking address (Guardian) is safer than locking accounts, because attackers can lock a real account on purpose.

audit_failures_off.title: Failed logons are not audited
audit_failures_off.fix: Without them PacketWard cannot see password guessing. Run: auditpol /set /subcategory:"Logon" /success:enable /failure:enable

audit_success_off.title: Successful logons are not audited
audit_success_off.fix: Without them PacketWard cannot learn which addresses are yours. Run: auditpol /set /subcategory:"Logon" /success:enable /failure:enable

only_administrators.title: The group “Remote Desktop Users” is empty
only_administrators.fix: Only administrators can connect. Give other people their own accounts in that group instead of sharing the administrator password.

restrict.title: Restrict Remote Desktop to trusted addresses
restrict.hint: Creates PacketWard rules that allow the RDP port only from these addresses. Every address that has logged in successfully is always included, so you cannot lock yourself out with this. The built-in Windows rules (which allow everybody) stay on unless you turn them off here.
restrict.allowed: Extra addresses or ranges (one per line)
restrict.disableBuiltin: Also turn off the built-in Remote Desktop rules (they allow everybody)

port.title: Change the RDP port
port.hint: Moves Remote Desktop to another port and opens it in the firewall first. The service restarts and every session is disconnected: reconnect to the new port and confirm.
port.understand: I understand that every Remote Desktop session will be disconnected and that I must reconnect to the new port.

nla.title: Network Level Authentication
nla.hint: Makes clients authenticate before a session exists. Recommended; only clients that support NLA can connect.

attempts.title: Attempt limit per address
attempts.hint: How many failed logons from one address, within how many seconds, count as password guessing.
attempts.guardian: The Guardian then blocks that address for a limited time (see the Guardian page). Addresses with a successful logon are never blocked.

lockout.title: Windows account lockout
lockout.warning: Off by default. An attacker can lock a legitimate account on purpose, which is a denial of service. PacketWard prefers blocking the attacking address.
lockout.understand: I understand that attackers can lock real accounts.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.confirmLogoff: Log this session off (unsaved work is lost)?

recovery.title: If you lose access
recovery.hint: Every change reverts by itself if you do not confirm it. If Remote Desktop still stops working, open your provider’s VNC / console, sign in there and run this in an administrator shell. It restores port 3389, the built-in rules and removes PacketWard’s restrictions.
recovery.reset: Restore Remote Desktop to factory settings
recovery.confirm: Restore the default port, the built-in rules and remove PacketWard’s RDP rules?

country.title: Country restriction
country.hint: Optional. When an address from a refused country connects to Remote Desktop, the Guardian blocks it. It reacts after the first connection (Windows Firewall cannot filter by country), only while the Guardian is Active, and never touches protected addresses.
country.searchPlaceholder: Name or code, for example Spain or ES
country.noGeo: The GeoIP database is not installed, so nothing is blocked. Download it in Threat intelligence.
country.emptyAllow: Allow-only mode needs at least one country, or every connection would be refused.
country.locksYouOut: You are connected from {countries}, which is not in the list: you would lock yourself out. Add it first.
country.monitor: The Guardian is not Active: the restriction only records what it would block.
country.activity: Last 24 hours: {blocked} blocked, {would} would have been blocked.

speed.title: Speed test
speed.hint: Measures latency, jitter and download/upload speed against a speed server. Tests never write to disk.
speed.serversHint: Your own speed-server, as https://host:port (http:// only for your own lab). XeroHost nodes appear here automatically once published.
speed.confirm50: I understand the 50 GB test moves 50 GB of data and can take a long time; it counts against my bandwidth and the server’s limits.
speed.empty: No results yet. Add a server and run a quick test.

errors.no_server: No server answered. Check the address, or add another server.
errors.confirmation_required: The 50 GB test needs the confirmation box ticked.
errors.rate_limited: The server is limiting this machine. Try again in {retry} seconds.
errors.budget_exceeded: This test would exceed the server’s transfer limit for your address. Try a smaller test later.
errors.invalid: A setting or a server address is not valid.
errors.unsupported: This agent cannot run speed tests; update it.
errors.busy: A speed test is already running.

geo.title: GeoIP database
geo.hint: Country and network (ASN) of remote addresses, looked up locally on this server. Nothing about your traffic is sent anywhere; only the database file is downloaded.

countries.title: Where connections come from
countries.hint: Countries of the remote addresses connected to this server right now.
countries.noDb: Download the GeoIP database to see countries.
countries.empty: No public remote addresses right now.

lists.title: Blocklists
lists.hint: Public lists of hostile networks. They are downloaded only when you switch them on, never contain your own protected addresses, and are removed from the firewall when you switch them off.
lists.confirm: This adds Windows Firewall block rules for every network in the list. Your gateway, DNS servers, RDP clients and allowlist are never blocked. Switch it on?

abuse.title: AbuseIPDB reputation (optional)
abuse.hint: With your own AbuseIPDB key you can check how often an address was reported. Without a key nothing is ever sent.
abuse.privacy: The key is kept in Windows Credential Manager. Only the public address you check is sent; private addresses never are.

map.title: Where attacks come from
map.hint: Countries of the addresses behind alerts and blocks. The darker, the more addresses. Location comes from the local GeoIP database.
map.noDb: Download the GeoIP database to see the map and the country flags.
map.failed: The map could not be loaded.
map.gestures: Scroll to zoom, drag to move

logs.title: Audit log
logs.hint: Every action PacketWard took or refused: blocks, unblocks, blocklists, Guardian decisions and Remote Desktop changes. Newest first.
logs.truncated: More entries match than are shown. Narrow the filter.

ipDetail.title: Details of {addr}
ipDetail.nothing: Nothing noteworthy: not blocked, not protected, no alerts.
ipDetail.abuseOff: Add an AbuseIPDB key in Threat intelligence to look addresses up. Nothing is sent without it.
ipDetail.noGeo: No GeoIP database: download it in Threat intelligence
